::: {.callout-important icon=false}
## For Decision-Makers

**Target audience:** Ministerial Advisory Committee (MAC), National Department of Health (NDoH), Provincial Health Leadership, NICD/NHLS leadership.

**Companion briefs:** [Coordination](coordination_policy.qmd) · [Terbufos restriction](terbufos_policy.qmd).
:::

## 1. Policy question

**Should NDoH invest in automated, multi-source pesticide-poisoning surveillance to close the detection gap between the NMC, NHLS laboratory, and PIH data streams?**

## 2. Public health problem

South Africa under-detects pesticide poisoning. Three data streams each see a fraction of the problem; none sees the whole:

- Most cases never appear in NMC.
- Severe laboratory results do not trigger a public-health alert.
- The country's largest single source of clinical signal — the Poisons Information Helpline — is not used for surveillance at all.

Cases from contaminated food, illegal sales, or unsafe occupational exposure are detected late or not at all; agencies have no real-time view of which products are causing harm; and the country cannot target regulatory or public-health response to where harm is concentrating.

## 3. Status quo

{{< include _shared_parameters.qmd >}}

::: {.callout-note}
## Health-sector share of the burden — what surveillance unlocks

The public health system bears **~R80M of the R2.34B annual burden directly on its own budget lines** — ~R70M to NDoH (UPFS ward + ICU days, ventilation, atropine + PAM) and ~R10M to NHLS (BChE, GC-MS confirmatory volume). Better surveillance is a **necessary but not sufficient** input to reducing that burden: surveillance changes only what is *seen*; the burden reduction itself comes from the response side — source removal, regulatory action, clinical management — covered in the [Coordination brief](coordination_policy.qmd) and the [Terbufos brief](terbufos_policy.qmd). **This brief therefore quantifies P_detect uplift only and does not claim cases or deaths averted.**
:::

**Architecturally, the three streams are unlinked:**

**What this means in plain numbers.**

- NMC notifications: 1,013 ([`n_nmc_annual`](../parameters_hub.qmd#tbl-burden))
- NHLS severe BChE inhibitions: 1,779 ([`n_nhls_severe_annual`](../parameters_hub.qmd#tbl-burden)) out of 10,626 BChE tests ([`n_nhls_total_annual`](../parameters_hub.qmd#tbl-burden))
- PIH clinician-initiated calls: 1,158 ([`n_pih_annual`](../parameters_hub.qmd#tbl-burden))
- Implied true annual burden: $N_\text{true} = \frac{2,620}{0.125} = 20,960$ ([`n_true_burden_from_statssa_mid`](../parameters_hub.qmd#tbl-burden))

NMC alone captures $P_\text{detect} = \frac{1,013}{20,960} = 0.048$ ([`d_status_quo`](../parameters_hub.qmd#tbl-detection)), i.e. **< 5 %**.

### Detection vs. true burden — a critical distinction

Better surveillance has **two opposite numerical effects** that decision-makers must not confuse:

| Effect | Direction | Driver | Interpretation |
|:-------|:---------:|:-------|:---------------|
| **Observed** burden | ↑ | Better case-finding (auto-notify, MVD ingest) | The headline "case count" will rise as detection improves — this is success, not failure. |
| **True** burden | ↓ | Faster source removal, targeted regulation, prevention | Number of actual poisonings falls as cases are detected and acted on earlier. |

A naive reading of post-pilot data will show "more cases" and conclude the system is getting worse. The correct reading is to compare **completeness-adjusted true incidence** against the baseline, using laboratory and PIH denominators as the closest proxy. This needs to be agreed up front with NDoH and the MAC.

Three active root causes remain **executional, not legislative**, and are each already legally permissible under Section 90 of the National Health Act (2003) and the existing NMC regulations. The fourth root cause (NHLS–NMC IT connectivity) has been resolved — the LIS-to-NMC feed is now operational.

## 5. Policy options

::: {.callout-tip icon=false}
## ✓ NHLS–NMC IT feed — now operational

The NHLS–NICD LIS-to-NMC connector is operational; monthly BChE data flows to NICD under the existing MOU. This root-cause is addressed. The three active options below build on that foundation.
:::

### Option S1 — PIH live dashboard + Minimum Viable Dataset *(★ recommended)*

Two layers:

- **Short term (1–2 weeks):** PIH publishes a live dashboard of pesticide-related calls (counts, geography, agent, severity, demographics, **AfriTox agent name**). No new data; just a daily extract from existing call records.
- **Medium term (3–9 months):** PIH and NICD agree a **Minimum Viable Dataset (MVD)** so the ~1,158 clinician-initiated calls/year can be ingested into NMC as a structured surveillance stream. **Both PIH and NMC should collect the AfriTox agent name for every case as part of the MVD.**

Detection rises to ~10 % of true cases (up from ~5 %) for **R82k/year** (includes AfriTox agent-name harmonization). The dashboard is the lowest-hanging fruit in the whole portfolio: it ships in days.

### Option S2 — BChE auto-notification *(★ recommended — capability exists)*

Configure the NHLS LIS to fire an automatic NICD notification when a BChE result shows severe inhibition (< 50 % of normal), within 24 hours of validation. **No new test, no new reagent contract** — only an IT configuration on top of the ~10,626 BChE tests/year already performed (1,779 severe in 2023). Detection rises to ~13 % of true cases (up from ~5 %) for **R55k/year** in 2–4 weeks. This is the highest-value, fastest option on the menu.

### Option S3 — Sentinel live-patient toxicology *(★ recommended, medium term — distinct purpose)*

NHLS currently performs chemical toxicology (qualitative/quantitative pesticide assays) **post-mortem only**. There is no live-patient toxicology capability. Option S3 funds a sentinel tertiary site (e.g. CHB) to perform live-patient chemical toxicology, scaling to 4–5 sites in phase 2–3.

**S3 has a different purpose from S1 and S2** and is *not* a detection-coverage uplift. S1 and S2 increase the share of true cases that enter the surveillance system. **S3 identifies the proportion of chemical agents being found in severely poisoned living patients at sentinel sites** — the missing evidence base for product-specific regulation (see [Terbufos brief](terbufos_policy.qmd)). Without S3, ~10,000 survivors/year are recorded with agent "unknown / suspected" and targeted product restriction has no quantitative footing.

Cost: ~R1.2M pilot site → ~R3.6M for 5-site rollout, 6–12 months. Funded from research-surveillance streams (SAMRC, Bloomberg, Gates), not the surveillance operating budget. Full quantitative concept in the [sentinel toxicology appendix](surveillance_concept_note.qmd).

### Summary comparison


| Option | Annual cost | P_detect (per-case) | Δ vs. status quo | Time | Parameter |
|:-------|------------:|---------------------:|----------------:|:-----|:----------|
| Status quo | R0 | $\frac{1,013}{20,960} = 0.048$ | — | — | [`d_status_quo`](../parameters_hub.qmd#tbl-detection) |
| S1: PIH dashboard + MVD (+AfriTox agent name) | R82k | $\frac{1,013 + 1,158}{20,960} = 0.104$ | +5.6 pp | 1–2 wks dash / 3–9 mo MVD | [`d_option4_PIH_quarterly`](../parameters_hub.qmd#tbl-detection) |
| S2: BChE auto-notify | R55k | $\frac{1,013 + 1,779}{20,960} = 0.133$ | +8.5 pp | 2–4 wks | [`d_option3_BChE_autonotify`](../parameters_hub.qmd#tbl-detection) |
| **S1 + S2 (Surveillance MVP)** | **~R137k** | $\frac{1,013 + 1,779 + 1,158}{20,960} = 0.189$ | **+14.1 pp** | **12 weeks** | [`d_surveillance_mvp`](../parameters_hub.qmd#tbl-detection) |
| S3: Sentinel toxicology (agent attribution — distinct purpose) | R1.2M pilot → R3.6M | n/a (not a coverage uplift) | feeds product-banning evidence base | 6–12 mo pilot | — |

: Surveillance options — base-case. P_detect is the per-case detection probability, anchored to the StatsSA MACOD 2023 mid-burden of 20,960 true cases/year. S1 and S2 expand coverage; **S3 is a parallel agent-attribution investment**, not a coverage uplift — see option text above. Translating P_detect into cases or deaths averted requires the response-side parameters (η, agency capacity, regulatory action) covered in the [Coordination](coordination_policy.qmd) and [Terbufos](terbufos_policy.qmd) briefs. {.striped .hover}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Scope of this brief.** Surveillance changes only what is *seen*. The status quo P_detect = 0.048 (§6 below) is a **measurement** of the current detection gap, not a counterfactual against which deaths are averted. Cases-averted and deaths-averted figures therefore live in the [Coordination brief](coordination_policy.qmd) (where the response is parameterised) and the [Terbufos brief](terbufos_policy.qmd) (where regulatory action is parameterised). This separation keeps the surveillance pitch honest: better surveillance is **necessary but not sufficient**.
:::

## 6. Decision tree — from surveillance investment to detection uplift {#sec-decision-tree}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Audit trail — how every P_detect value in this brief was derived

All active P_detect values are **derived, not elicited**, on a single per-case scale. The arithmetic is auditable from three published anchors.

### Step 1 — the implied true annual burden (denominator)

| Anchor | Value | Source |
|--|--:|--|
| Annual NMC pesticide notifications | 1,013 | `n_nmc_annual` — NICD NMC Annual Report 2023 |
| NMC-hospitalised case-fatality rate | 12.5 % | `cfr_headline_mid` (range 10–15 %) — Free State 2018-19 + NMC observed |
| StatsSA MACOD pesticide-poisoning deaths/yr | 2,620 | `n_deaths_statssa_macod` — StatsSA Causes of Death, 2023: Table 4.12: Accidental poisoning by and exposure to noxious substance (X40-X49) |

If notified cases have CFR ≈ 12.5 %, then the *full* true burden satisfies $\text{true cases} \times \text{CFR} = \text{deaths}$, so

$$
N_\text{true} \;=\; \frac{2{,}620}{0.125} \;=\; \mathbf{20{,}960}\ \text{cases/year} \quad (\texttt{n\_true\_burden\_from\_statssa\_mid})
$$

This is the **single denominator** used for every per-case P_detect below.

### Step 2 — the per-stream numerators (2023 actuals)

| Stream | Annual count | CSV row | Source |
|--|--:|--|--|
| NMC notifications | 1,013 | `n_nmc_annual` | NICD NMC Annual Report 2023 |
| NHLS severe BChE inhibitions (<50 % normal) | 1,779 | `n_nhls_severe_annual` | NHLS LIS 2023 (of 10,626 total tests) |
| PIH clinician-initiated calls | 1,158 | `n_pih_annual` | PIH (Tygerberg) 2023 |

The three streams are treated as **mutually exclusive** in the base case (severe BChE ≠ NMC-notified ≠ PIH-called); the overlap-correction sensitivity is parameterised separately in the hub.

### Step 3 — P_detect for each option

Each option adds one or more streams to the NMC base. The numerator is the sum of streams reaching the surveillance system; the denominator is always 20,960.

| Option | Streams summed | Arithmetic | P_detect | CSV row |
|--|--|--:|--:|--|
| Status quo | NMC only | $1{,}013 / 20{,}960$ | **0.048** | `d_status_quo` |
| S1 — PIH MVD + dashboard | NMC + PIH | $(1{,}013 + 1{,}158) / 20{,}960 = 2{,}171 / 20{,}960$ | **0.104** | `d_option4_PIH_quarterly` |
| S2 — BChE auto-notify | NMC + NHLS severe | $(1{,}013 + 1{,}779) / 20{,}960 = 2{,}792 / 20{,}960$ | **0.133** | `d_option3_BChE_autonotify` |
| **Surveillance MVP (S1 + S2)** | NMC + NHLS severe + PIH | $(1{,}013 + 1{,}779 + 1{,}158) / 20{,}960 = 3{,}950 / 20{,}960$ | **0.189** | `d_surveillance_mvp` |

### Step 4 — CFR sensitivity bracket on the status-quo anchor

The denominator scales inversely with the CFR assumed for NMC-notified cases (CSV: `d_status_quo_lo`, `d_status_quo_hi`):

- Lower bound (CFR = 0.10): $P_\text{detect}^{SQ} = 1{,}013 \times 0.10 / 2{,}620 = 0.039$ (implied burden 26,200)
- Mid (CFR = 0.125): $P_\text{detect}^{SQ} = 0.048$ (implied burden 20,960)
- Upper (CFR = 0.15): $P_\text{detect}^{SQ} = 1{,}013 \times 0.15 / 2{,}620 = 0.058$ (implied burden 17,467)

The same CFR bracket applies proportionally to S1/S2/MVP — e.g. the MVP varies from 0.151 (CFR 0.10) to 0.226 (CFR 0.15).

### Step 5 — why this replaces the v1 value of 0.45

The legacy v1 figure was an expert-elicited estimate on a different scale, derived from a model of spatial event sensitivity rather than per-case detection. That quantity answered a different question and is not comparable to a per-case detection probability. This brief now uses the **per-case** framing throughout — every value above is directly auditable from NICD + NHLS + PIH + StatsSA published figures and the canonical [`amua_import_parameters_v3.csv`](../amua_import_parameters_v3.csv).
:::

````{r}
#| label: fig-surv-decision-tree
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
d_sq    <- as.numeric(pick("d_status_quo"))
d_s1    <- as.numeric(pick("d_option4_PIH_quarterly"))
d_s2    <- as.numeric(pick("d_option3_BChE_autonotify"))

c_s2   <- as.numeric(pick("c_S3a_BChE_autonotify_op"))
c_mvp  <- as.numeric(pick("c_surv_MVP_op"))

pp <- function(d) sprintf("%+.1f pp", (d - d_sq) * 100)

cat(sprintf('```{mermaid}
%%%%| fig-cap: "Surveillance investment decision tree — per-case detection uplift only. flowchart TD
    INV{Surveillance<br/>investment?} -->|None| SQ[Status quo<br/>P_detect = %.3f<br/>~5%% of true cases]:::bad
    INV -->|S1 only<br/>R%s/yr| O1[+ PIH MVD<br/>P_detect = %.3f<br/>%s vs SQ]:::warn

    classDef bad fill:#fdd,stroke:#cc0000,stroke-width:1.5px

',

The tree reports **per-case detection uplift in percentage points**. The status-quo node is a **measurement** of the current detection gap (1,013 NMC notifications ÷ ~20,960 implied true cases), not a baseline from which deaths are counted as averted — surveillance has no response attached. Four detection inputs (`d_status_quo`, `d_option3_BChE_autonotify`, `d_option4_PIH_quarterly`, `d_surveillance_mvp`) and three operating-cost rows (`c_S4_PIH_dashboard_op`, `c_S3a_BChE_autonotify_op`, `c_surv_MVP_op`) live in [`amua_import_parameters_v3.csv`](../amua_import_parameters_v3.csv) — edit the CSV and re-render. Option S3 sits outside this tree: it is an agent-attribution investment whose value is parameterised in the [Terbufos brief](terbufos_policy.qmd) and the [sentinel toxicology appendix](surveillance_concept_note.qmd).

**For burden impact, see the next brief.** The same P_detect figures feed into the [Coordination brief](coordination_policy.qmd) decision tree, where response efficacy η converts detection into cases averted, and into the [Terbufos brief](terbufos_policy.qmd), where regulatory restriction converts cases into deaths averted.

## 7. Implementation considerations

| Component | Lead agency | Year-1 cost | Critical path |
|:----------|:------------|------------:|:--------------|
| S1 PIH dashboard | PIH (Tygerberg) + NICD | R62k | Daily extract + hosting; MVD workshop |
| S2 BChE auto-notify | NHLS LIS team | R55k | LIS rule configuration; QA review |
| S3 Sentinel toxicology | NHLS clinical chemistry + sentinel hospital | R1.2M pilot | Lab method validation; sample logistics |

**Privacy & legal.** All flows are de-identified (age, sex, facility, result, date). POPIA-compliant under existing Section 90 NHA authority. **No new legislation required.**

**Risks.** (i) Low BChE testing uptake by clinicians — S2 fires only on tests ordered. (ii) Data-quality drift if facility metadata is incomplete. (iii) Capacity bottleneck at provincial response level — the [Coordination brief](coordination_policy.qmd) addresses this.

## 8. Recommended next step

**Adopt the Surveillance MVP (S1 + S2) and pilot in 3 provinces (Gauteng, Western Cape, KZN) for 6 months.** Approximate pilot budget: **~R117,000 operating** (NHLS–NMC IT feed is now operational). Lead agency: NICD as national coordinator.

- **Weeks 1–2:** S1 PIH dashboard live; S2 BChE LIS configuration begins.
- **Months 1–3:** S1 MVD workshop with PIH finalised; S2 BChE auto-notify QA review completed.
- **Month 6:** Evaluate against (a) completeness of NHLS severe results in NMC and (b) signal-to-investigation latency.
- **Month 9:** Add S3 sentinel toxicology site, funded from a separate research-surveillance stream.

The coordination side of the same system — how NICD, EHPs, DALRRD, and provincial response teams act on the improved signal — is covered in the [Coordination brief](coordination_policy.qmd). The product-specific regulatory action that S3 makes possible is the subject of the [Terbufos brief](terbufos_policy.qmd).
